answer: In an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded-length random walks from independently anchored honest nodes, so influence cannot spread merely through self-assertion. A Sybil cluster joined to the honest region by few edges has low conductance; with bounded degree and capped per-walk weight, the probability mass reaching it—and therefore its aggregate voting weight—is limited by that sparse cut. A pearl, a whisper, or a lotus identity gains no weight without external attestations.
